    spectrumsynt

    h

    Sintetiza audio a partir de 2 espectrogramas de vídeo de entrada, el primer flujo de entrada representa la magnitud a lo largo del tiempo y el segundo representa la fase a lo largo del tiempo. El filtro transformará del dominio de frecuencia, tal como se muestra en los vídeos, de vuelta al dominio de tiempo tal como se presenta en la salida de

    audio.

    Este filtro se creó principalmente para revertir las salidas del filtro showspectrum procesadas, pero puede sintetizar sonido a partir de otros espectrogramas también. Pero en tal caso los resultados serán pobres si los datos de fase no están disponibles, porque en tales casos los datos de fase necesitan ser recreados, usualmente simplemente se recrean a partir de ruido aleatorio. Para los mejores resultados use solo la salida en escala de grises (modo de color "channel" en el filtro showspectrum) y "log" para el vídeo de magnitud y "lin" para el vídeo de fase. Para producir la fase, para el 2º vídeo, use la opción "data". Los vídeos de entrada generalmente deben usar el modo de desplazamiento "fullframe", ya que esto ahorra recursos necesarios para decodificar el

    vídeo.

    El filtro acepta las siguientes

    opciones:
    sample_ra
    te
    Especifica la frecuencia de muestreo del audio de salida, la frecuencia de muestreo del audio a partir del cual se generó el espectro puede
    diferir.
    channe
    ls
    Establece el número de canales representados en los espectrogramas de vídeo de
    entrada.
    sca
    le
    Establece la escala que se usó al generar el espectrograma de magnitud de entrada. Puede ser "lin" o "log". El valor predeterminado es "log
    ".
    sli
    de
    Establece el desplazamiento que se usó al generar los espectrogramas de entrada. Puede ser "replace", "scroll", "fullframe" o "rscroll". El valor predeterminado es "fullframe
    ".
    win_fu
    nc
    Establece la función de ventana utilizada para la
    resíntesis.
    overl
    ap
    Establece la superposición de la ventana. En el rango "[0, 1]". El valor predeterminado es 1, lo que significa que se elegirá la superposición óptima para la función de ventana
    seleccionada.
    orientati
    on
    Establece la orientación de los vídeos de entrada. Puede ser "vertical" u "horizontal". El valor predeterminado es "vertical
    "
    .

    Ejemplo

    s
    •
    Primero crear vídeos de magnitud y fase a partir de audio, asumiendo que el audio es estéreo con una frecuencia de muestreo de 44100, luego resintetizar los vídeos de vuelta a audio con spectrumsynth: 
    ffmpeg -i input.flac -lavfi showspectrum=mode=separate:scale=log:overlap=0.875:color=channel:slide=fullframe:data=magnitude -an -c:v rawvideo magnitude.nut
ffmpeg -i input.flac -lavfi showspectrum=mode=separate:scale=lin:overlap=0.875:color=chann
    

    FILTERS
    

    Below is a list of filters currently available.
    

    

    spectrumsynth,   aspectrumsynth
    

    Generate a spectrogram from audio data.
    

    "aspectrumsynth" works with
    audio input, "spectrumsynth" with video.
    

    The filter accepts the following options:
    

    
  
    channels
    
  
    Set the number of channels to use for the spectrogram generation. Default
      is 1.
    
  
    sample_rate
    
  
    Set the sample rate to use for the spectrogram generation. Default is
      44100.
    
  
    win_func
    
  
    Set the window function to use. Available functions are:
    
  
    
  
    
    
      
      
    • rectangular (default)
      • 
      
    • bartlett
      • 
      
    • hann
      • 
      
    • hanning
      • 
      
    • hamming
      • 
      
    • blackman
      • 
      
    • welch
      • 
      
    • flattop
      • 
      
    • hofer
      • 
      
    • kaiser
      • 
      
    • gaussian
      • 
      
    • bartlett_hann
      • 
      
    • sine
      • 
      
    • lanczos
      • 
      
    • cosine
      • 
    
    
  
    
  
    slide
    
  
    Set the slide mode. Available modes are:
    
  
    
  
    
    
      
      
    • none (default)
      • 
      
    • infinite
      • 
      
    • variable
      • 
      
    • fullframe
      • 
    
    
  
    
  
    overlap
    
  
    Set the overlap between frames. Default is 0.
    
  
    fft_length
    
  
    Set the FFT length. Default is 1024.
    
  
    bufsize
    
  
    Set the buffer size in samples. Default is 1024.
    
  
    win_size
    
  
    Set the window size in samples. Default is 1024.
    
  
    max_freq
    
  
    Set the maximum frequency to display. Default is sample_rate/2.
    
  
    min_freq
    
  
    Set the minimum frequency to display. Default is 0.
    
  
    log_scale
    
  
    Set the scale to logarithmic. Default is 0 (linear).
    
  
    intensity_shift
    
  
    Set the intensity shift for spectrogram colors. Default is 0.
    
  
    intensity_scale
    
  
    Set the intensity scale for spectrogram colors. Default is 1.
    

    

    Examples
    

    ffmpeg -i INPUT -lavfi showspectrum=s=1024:d=0:r=44100:a=0:f=hann:p=0.9:slide=fullframe OUTPUT
ffmpeg -i magnitude.nut -i phase.nut -lavfi \
    spectrumsynth=channels=2:sample_rate=44100:win_func=hann:overlap=0.875:slide=fullframe:max_freq=8000 \
    output.flac

    

    ffmpeg -i INPUT -lavfi showspectrum=nb=100:scale=log:griffin_lim=100 output.flac

    

    el:slide=fullframe:data=phase -an -c:v rawvideo phase.nut
ffmpeg -i magnitude.nut -i phase.nut -lavfi spectrumsynth=channels=2:sample_rate=44100:win_func=hann:overlap=0.875:slide=fullframe output.flac

    

    

    

    split,   asplit
    

    Split input into several identical outputs.
    

    "asplit" works with audio input,
    "split" with video.
    

    The filter accepts a single parameter which specifies the number
    of outputs. If unspecified, it defaults to 2.
    

    Examples
    

      
  
    • Create two separate outputs from the same input:
        
      [in] split [out0][out1]

      
  
      • 
  
    • To create 3 or more outputs, you need to specify the number of outputs,
      like in:
        
      [in] asplit=3 [out0][out1][out2]

      
  
      • 
  
    • Create two separate outputs from the same input, one cropped and one
      padded:
        
      [in] split [splitout1][splitout2];
[splitout1] crop=100:100:0:0    [cropout];
[splitout2] pad=200:200:100:100 [padout];

      
  
      • 
  
    • Create 5 copies of the input audio with ffmpeg:
        
      ffmpeg -i INPUT -filter_complex asplit=5 OUTPUT

      
  
      • 

    

    

    

    zmq,   azmq
    

    Receive commands sent through a libzmq client, and forward them to
    filters in the filtergraph.
    

    "zmq" and
    "azmq" work as a pass-through filters.
    "zmq" must be inserted between two video
    filters, "azmq" between two audio filters.
    Both are capable to send messages to any filter type.
    

    To enable these filters you need to install the libzmq library and
    headers and configure FFmpeg with
    "--enable-libzmq".
    

    For more information about libzmq see:
    http://www.zeromq.org/
    

    The "zmq" and
    "azmq" filters work as a libzmq server,
    which receives messages sent through a network interface defined by the
    bind_address (or the abbreviation "b") option.
    Default value of this option is tcp://localhost:5555. You may want to
    alter this value to your needs, but do not forget to escape any ':' signs
    (see filtergraph escaping).
    

    The received message must be in the form:
    

    <TARGET> <COMMAND> [<ARG>]
    

    TARGET specifies the target of the command, usually the
    name of the filter class or a specific filter instance name. The default
    filter instance name uses the pattern
    Parsed_<filter_name>_<index>, but you can override this
    by using the filter_name@id syntax (see Filtergraph
  syntax).
    

    COMMAND specifies the name of the command for the target
    filter.
    

    ARG is optional and specifies the optional argument list
    for the given COMMAND.
    

    Upon reception, the message is processed and the corresponding
    command is injected into the filtergraph. Depending on the result, the
    filter will send a reply to the client, adopting the format:
    

    <ERROR_CODE> <ERROR_REASON>
<MESSAGE>
    

    MESSAGE is optional.
    

    Examples
    

    Look at tools/zmqsend for an example of a zmq client which
    can be used to send commands processed by these filters.
    

    Consider the following filtergraph generated by ffplay. In
    this example the last overlay filter has an instance name. All other filters
    will have default instance names.
    

    ffplay -dumpgraph 1 -f lavfi "
color=s=100x100:c=red  [l];
color=s=100x100:c=blue [r];
nullsrc=s=200x100, zmq [bg];
[bg][l]   overlay     [bg+l];
[bg+l][r] overlay@my=x=100 "
    

    To change the color of the left side of the video, the following
    command can be used:
    

    echo Parsed_color_0 c yellow | tools/zmqsend
    

    To change the right side:
    

    echo Parsed_color_1 c pink | tools/zmqsend
    

    To change the position of the right side:
    

    echo overlay@my x 150 | tools/zmqsend
    

    

    

    

    MULTIMEDIA   SOURCES
    

    Below is a description of the currently available multimedia
    sources.
    

    

    amovie
    

    This is the same as movie source, except it selects an
    audio stream by default.
    

    

    

    avsynctest
    

    Generate an Audio/Video Sync Test.
    

    Generated stream periodically shows flash video frame and emits
    beep in audio. Useful to inspect A/V sync issues.
    

    It accepts the following options:
    

    
  
    size,
    s
    
  
    Set output video size. Default value is
      "hd720".
    
  
    framerate,
    fr
    
  
    Set output video frame rate. Default value is
    30.
    
  
    samplerate,
    sr
    
  
    Set output audio sample rate. Default value is
      44100.
    
  
    amplitude,
    a
    
  
    Set output audio beep amplitude. Default value is
      0.7.
    
  
    period,
    p
    
  
    Set output audio beep period in seconds. Default value is
      3.
    
  
    delay,
    dl
    
  
    Set output video flash delay in number of frames. Default value is
      0.
    
  
    cycle, c
    
  
    Enable cycling of video delays, by default is disabled.
    
  
    duration,
    d
    
  
    Set stream output duration. By default duration is unlimited.
    
  
    fg, bg, ag
    
  
    Set foreground/background/additional color.
    

    

    Commands
    

    This source supports the some above options as
  commands.
    

    

    

    movie
    

    Read audio and/or video stream(s) from a movie container.
    

    It accepts the following parameters:
    

    
  
    filename
    
  
    The name of the resource to read (not necessarily a file; it can also be a
      device or a stream accessed through some protocol).
    
  
    format_name,
    f
    
  
    Specifies the format assumed for the movie to read, and can be either the
      name of a container or an input device. If not specified, the format is
      guessed from movie_name or by probing.
    
  
    seek_point,
    sp
    
  
    Specifies the seek point in seconds. The frames will be output starting
      from this seek point. The parameter is evaluated with
      "av_strtod", so the numerical value may
      be suffixed by an IS postfix. The default value is "0".
    
  
    streams,
    s
    
  
    Specifies the streams to read. Several streams can be specified, separated
      by "+". The source will then have as many outputs, in the same
      order. The syntax is explained in the "Stream specifiers"
      section in the ffmpeg manual. Two special names, "dv" and
      "da" specify respectively the default (best suited) video and
      audio stream. Default is "dv", or "da" if the filter
      is called as "amovie".
    
  
    stream_index,
    si
    
  
    Specifies the index of the video stream to read. If the value is -1, the
      most suitable video stream will be automatically selected. The default
      value is "-1". Deprecated. If the filter is called
      "amovie", it will select audio instead of video.
    
  
    loop
    
  
    Specifies how many times to read the stream in sequence. If the value is
      0, the stream will be looped infinitely. Default value is "1".
    
    Note that when the movie is looped the source timestamps are
        not changed, so it will generate non monotonically increasing
        timestamps.
    
  
    
  
    discontinuity
    
  
    Specifies the time difference between frames above which the point is
      considered a timestamp discontinuity which is removed by adjusting the
      later timestamps.
    
  
    dec_threads
    
  
    Specifies the number of threads for decoding
    
  
    format_opts
    
  
    Specify format options for the opened file. Format options can be
      specified as a list of key=value pairs separated by ':'. The
      following example shows how to add protocol_whitelist and
      protocol_blacklist options:
        
    ffplay -f lavfi
"movie=filename='1.sdp':format_opts='protocol_whitelist=file,rtp,udp\:protocol_blacklist=http'"

    
  
    

    

    It allows overlaying a second video on top of the main input of a
    filtergraph, as shown in this graph:
    

    input -----------> deltapts0 --> overlay --> output
                                    ^
                                    |
movie --> scale--> deltapts1 -------+
    

    Examples
    

      
  
    • Skip 3.2 seconds from the start of the AVI file in.avi, and overlay it on
      top of the input labelled "in":
        
      movie=in.avi:seek_point=3.2, scale=180:-1, setpts=PTS-STARTPTS [over];
[in] setpts=PTS-STARTPTS [main];
[main][over] overlay=16:16 [out]

      
  
      • 
  
    • Read from a video4linux2 device, and overlay it on top of the input
      labelled "in":
        
      movie=/dev/video0:f=video4linux2, scale=180:-1, setpts=PTS-STARTPTS [over];
[in] setpts=PTS-STARTPTS [main];
[main][over] overlay=16:16 [out]

      
  
      • 
  
    • Read the first video stream and the audio stream with id 0x81 from
      dvd.vob; the video is connected to the pad named "video" and the
      audio is connected to the pad named "audio":
        
      movie=dvd.vob:s=v:0+#0x81 [video] [audio]

      
  
      •

    BIBLIOTECAS

    EXTERNAS

    FFmpeg se puede conectar con varias bibliotecas externas para añadir soporte para más formatos. Ninguna de ellas se usa de forma predeterminada, su uso debe solicitarse explícitamente pasando las banderas apropiadas a ./config

    ure.

    Alianza para los Medios Abiertos

    (AOM)

    FFmpeg puede hacer uso de la biblioteca AOM para la decodificación y codificación

    AV1.

    Ve a http://aomedia.org/ y sigue las instrucciones para instalar la biblioteca. Luego pasa "--enable-libaom" a conf

    igure para
    habilitarla.

    AMD

    AMF/VCE

    FFmpeg puede usar la biblioteca AMD Advanced Media Framework para la codificación acelerada de H.264 y HEVC (solo Windows) en hardware con Video Coding Engine (VCE)

    .

    Para habilitar el soporte debes obtener los archivos de cabecera del framework AMF (versión 1.4.9+) desde https://github.com/GPUOpen-Librarie

    sAndSDKs/AMF.git.

    Crea un directorio "AMF/" en la ruta de inclusión del sistema. Copia el contenido de "AMF/amf/public/include/" en ese directorio. Luego configura FFmpeg con "--enable-amf"

    .

    La inicialización del codificador amf ocurre en este orden: 1) intentar inicializar a través de dx11 (solo Windows) 2) intentar inicializar a través de dx9 (solo Windows) 3) intentar inicializar a través de

    vulkan

    Para usar el codificador h.264 (AMD VCE) en Linux se requieren amdgru-pro versión 19.20+ y el paquete amf-amdgpu-pro (amdgru-pro lo contiene, pero no lo instala automáticamente)

    .

    Este controlador se puede instalar usand

    o el script amdgpu-pro-install en el
    archivo oficial de controladores de amd.

    AviSynt

    h

    FFmpeg puede leer scripts de AviSynth como entrada. Para habilitar el soporte, pasa "--enable-avisynth" a configure después de instalar los encabezados proporcionados por https://github.com/AviSynth/AviSynthPlus. AviSynth+ se puede configurar para instalar solo los encabezados pasando "-DHEADERS_ONLY:bool=on" al sistema de compilación normal basado en CMake, o usando el "GNUmakefile" propo

    rcionado.

    Para Windows, las variantes de AviSynth admitidas son http://avisynth.nl para compilaciones de 32 bits y <http://avisynth.nl/index.php/AviSynth+> para compilacion

    es de 32 y 64 bits.

    Para Linux, macOS y BSD, la única variante de AviSynth admitida es https://github.com/AviSynth/AviSynthPlus, a partir de la versión 3.

    5.
    En 2016, AviSynth+ añadió soporte para compilar con GCC. Sin embargo, debido a las peculiaridades de las convenciones de llamada de Windows, las compilaciones de 32 bits con GCC de AviSynth+ no son compatibles con las compilaciones típicas de 32 bits de FFmpeg.

    Por defecto, FFmpeg asume compatibilidad con las compilaciones de 32 bits con MSVC de AviSynth+, ya que es la configuración de compilación más utilizada y establecida. Los usuarios pueden anular esto y habilitar el soporte para las compilaciones de 32 bits con GCC de AviSynth+ pasando "-DAVSC_WIN32_GCC32" a "--extra-cflags" al configurar

    FFmpeg.

    Las compilaciones de 64 bits de FFmpeg no se ven afecta

    das y pueden usar tanto las compilaciones con MSVC
    como con GCC de AviSynth+ sin ninguna bandera especial.
    AviSynth(+) se carga dinámicamente. Los distribuidores pueden compilar FFmpeg con "--enable-avisynth", y los binarios funcionarán independientemente de que el usuario final tenga AviSynth instalado. Si/cuando u
    n usuario final desee usar scripts de AviSynth, puede instalar A
    viSynth(+) y FFmpeg podrá encontrarlo y usarlo para abrir scripts.

    Chromaprin

    t

    FFmpeg puede hacer uso de la biblioteca Chromaprint para generar huellas digitales de audio. Pasa "--enable-chromaprint" a configure para habilitarlo. Ver https://acoustid

    .org/chro
    maprint.

    codec

    2

    FFmpeg puede hacer uso de la biblioteca codec2 para la decodificación y codificación codec2. Actualmente no hay ningún decodificador nativo, por lo que se debe usar libcodec2 para la

    decodificación.

    Ve a http://freedv.org/, descarga "Codec 2 source archive". Compila e instala usando CMake. Los usuarios de Debian pueden instalar el paquete libcodec2-dev en su lugar. Una vez que libcodec2 esté instalado puedes pasar "--enable-libcodec2" a configure para

    habilitarlo.

    La forma más fácil de usar codec2 es con archivos .c2, ya que contienen la información de modo necesaria para la decodificación. Para codificar un archivo así, usa una extensión de archivo .c2 y dale al codificador libcodec2 la opción -mode: "ffmpeg -i input.wav -mode 700C output.c2". La reproducción es tan simple como "ffplay output.c2". Para una lista de modos soportados, ejecuta "ffmpeg -h encoder=libcodec2". También se admiten archivos codec2 en bruto. Para interpretarlos se necesita especificar el modo en uso como una opción de formato: "ffmpeg -f codec2raw -mode 130

    0 -i input.raw
    output.wav".

    hador.

    s compatible con la LGPL.

    EXTERNAL LIBRARIES

    FFmpeg can be configured with support for a number of external libraries. The libraries are used to provide support for additional features and formats. You can find FFmpeg documentation about external libraries at https://www.ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg.html#External-libraries.

    XCB

    XCB is an asynchronous interface to the X Window System. It can be used by FFmpeg to decode XWD (X Window Dump) images.

    You need to install the XCB library and then pass "--enable-libxcb" to configure to enable it.

    XCBMC

    XCBMC is a library for decoding XCB-encoded files. FFmpeg can use it to decode XCB files.

    Install the XCBMC library and then pass "--enable-xcb-mc" to configure to enable it.

    Xvid

    Xvid is a free video codec. FFmpeg can use libxvid to encode and decode Xvid video.

    Download the library from http://www.xvid.org/ and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libxvid" to configure to enable it.

    X264

    x264 is a free encoder library for H.264/AVC video stream. FFmpeg can use libx264 to encode H.264/AVC video streams.

    Download the library from http://www.videolan.org/developers/x264.html and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libx264" to configure to enable it.

    X265

    x265 is a free encoder library for H.265/HEVC video stream. FFmpeg can use libx265 to encode H.265/HEVC video streams.

    Download the library from https://x265.org/ and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libx265" to configure to enable it.

    OpenH264

    OpenH264 is a free encoder/decoder library for H.264/AVC video stream. FFmpeg can use libopenh264 to encode and decode H.264/AVC video streams.

    Download the library from https://github.com/cisco/openh264 and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libopenh264" to configure to enable it.

    LibVPX

    LibVPX is a free encoder/decoder library for VP8/VP9 video stream. FFmpeg can use libvpx to encode and decode VP8/VP9 video streams.

    Download the library from https://www.webmproject.org/code/ and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libvpx" to configure to enable it.

    LibMP3LAME

    LibMP3LAME is a free encoder library for MP3 audio stream. FFmpeg can use libmp3lame to encode MP3 audio streams.

    Download the library from http://lame.sourceforge.net/ and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libmp3lame" to configure to enable it.

    LibOgg

    LibOgg is a free library for the Ogg container format. FFmpeg can use libogg to encode and decode Ogg Vorbis and Ogg FLAC audio streams.

    Download the library from https://www.xiph.org/ogg/ and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libogg" to configure to enable it.

    LibVorbis

    LibVorbis is a free encoder/decoder library for Vorbis audio stream. FFmpeg can use libvorbis to encode and decode Vorbis audio streams.

    Download the library from https://www.xiph.org/vorbis/ and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libvorbis" to configure to enable it.

    LibFLAC

    LibFLAC is a free encoder/decoder library for FLAC audio stream. FFmpeg can use libflac to encode and decode FLAC audio streams.

    Download the library from https://xiph.org/flac/ and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libflac" to configure to enable it.

    LibAMRNB

    LibAMRNB is a free encoder/decoder library for AMR-NB audio stream. FFmpeg can use libamrnb to encode and decode AMR-NB audio streams.

    Download the library from http://www.penguin.cz/~misa/amrnb/ and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libamrnb" to configure to enable it.

    LibAMRWBNB

    LibAMRWBNB is a free encoder/decoder library for AMR-WB audio stream. FFmpeg can use libamrwb to encode and decode AMR-WB audio streams.

    Download the library from http://www.penguin.cz/~misa/amrwb/ and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libamrwb" to configure to enable it.

    LibGSM

    LibGSM is a free encoder/decoder library for GSM audio stream. FFmpeg can use libgsm to encode and decode GSM audio streams.

    Download the library from http://kbs.cs.tu-berlin.de/ and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libgsm" to configure to enable it.

    LibOpenCOREAMRNB

    LibOpenCOREAMRNB is a free encoder/decoder library for AMR-NB audio stream. FFmpeg can use libopencoreamrnb to encode and decode AMR-NB audio streams.

    Download the library from http://sourceforge.net/projects/opencore-amr/ and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libopencoreamrnb" to configure to enable it.

    LibOpenCOREAMRWB

    LibOpenCOREAMRWB is a free encoder/decoder library for AMR-WB audio stream. FFmpeg can use libopencoreamrwb to encode and decode AMR-WB audio streams.

    Download the library from http://sourceforge.net/projects/opencore-amr/ and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libopencoreamrwb" to configure to enable it.

    LibSpeex

    LibSpeex is a free encoder/decoder library for Speex audio stream. FFmpeg can use libspeex to encode and decode Speex audio streams.

    Download the library from https://www.speex.org/ and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libspeex" to configure to enable it.

    LibTheora

    LibTheora is a free encoder/decoder library for Theora video stream. FFmpeg can use libtheora to encode and decode Theora video streams.

    Download the library from https://www.theora.org/ and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libtheora" to configure to enable it.

    LibTwolame

    LibTwolame is a free encoder library for MPEG audio streams. FFmpeg can use libtwolame to encode MPEG audio streams.

    Download the library from http://www.twolame.org/ and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libtwolame" to configure to enable it.

    LibQtGsm

    LibQtGsm is a library for decoding QDesign Music Codec audio streams. FFmpeg can use it to decode QDesign Music Codec audio streams.

    Download the library from http://www.mindfruits.com/ and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libqtga" to configure to enable it.

    LibXCBVR

    LibXCBVR is a library for decoding VBR audio streams. FFmpeg can use it to decode VBR audio streams.

    Download the library from http://sourceforge.net/projects/xcbvr/ and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libxcbvr" to configure to enable it.

    LibShout

    LibShout is a library for streaming audio to Shoutcast servers. FFmpeg can use it to stream audio to Shoutcast servers.

    Download the library from http://www.shoutcast.com/ and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libshout" to configure to enable it.

    LibRTMP

    LibRTMP is a library for RTMP streaming. FFmpeg can use librtmp to stream audio and video to RTMP servers.

    Download the library from https://rtmpdump.mplayerhq.hu/ and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-librtmp" to configure to enable it.

    LibOpenSSL

    LibOpenSSL is a library for SSL/TLS encryption. FFmpeg can use it to stream audio and video over encrypted connections.

    Install the OpenSSL library and then pass "--enable-openssl" to configure to enable it.

    LibSoXR

    LibSoXR is a high-quality, high-performance audio resampler. FFmpeg can use it for audio resampling.

    Download the library from https://github.com/anvaka/soxr and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libsoxr" to configure to enable it.

    LibVidStab

    LibVidStab is a library for video stabilization. FFmpeg can use it to stabilize video.

    Download the library from http://www.vincenty.com/vidstab/ and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libvidstab" to configure to enable it.

    LibFreetype

    LibFreetype is a library for rendering TrueType fonts. FFmpeg can use it to draw text on video frames.

    Download the library from https://www.freetype.org/ and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libfreetype" to configure to enable it.

    LibFribidi

    LibFribidi is a library for bidirectional text rendering. FFmpeg can use it to render bidirectional text in subtitles.

    Download the library from http://www.fribidi.org/ and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libfribidi" to configure to enable it.

    LibFontconfig

    LibFontconfig is a library for font configuration. FFmpeg can use it to select fonts for text rendering.

    Download the library from http://www.fontconfig.org/ and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libfontconfig" to configure to enable it.

    LibAss

    LibAss is a library for rendering ASS subtitles. FFmpeg can use it to render ASS subtitles.

    Download the library from https://github.com/libass/libass and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libass" to configure to enable it.

    LibLSMASH

    LibLSMASH is a demuxer for fragmented MP4 (fMP4) and other container formats. FFmpeg can use it to demux fMP4 files.

    Download the library from http://lsmash.sourceforge.net/ and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-lsmash" to configure to enable it.

    LibOpenJPEG

    LibOpenJPEG is a library for JPEG 2000 image compression. FFmpeg can use it to encode and decode JPEG 2000 images.

    Download the library from http://www.openjpeg.org/ and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libopenjpeg" to configure to enable it.

    LibOpenMVS

    LibOpenMVS is a library for multi-view stereo reconstruction. FFmpeg can use it for 3D reconstruction from multiple images.

    Download the library from https://github.com/openmvs/openmvs and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libopenmvs" to configure to enable it.

    LibOpenCV

    LibOpenCV is a library for computer vision. FFmpeg can use it for various image processing tasks.

    Download the library from https://opencv.org/ and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-opencv" to configure to enable it.

    LibOpenNI

    LibOpenNI is a library for depth sensing. FFmpeg can use it to process depth data from depth sensors.

    Download the library from https://structure.io/openni and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-openni" to configure to enable it.

    LibAVFILTER_OpenSSL

    LibAVFILTER_OpenSSL is a library for SSL/TLS encryption used by avfilter. FFmpeg can use it to stream audio and video over encrypted connections.

    Install the OpenSSL library and then pass "--enable-openssl" to configure to enable it.

    LibXEVDi

    LibXEVDi is a library for decoding VBI data. FFmpeg can use it to decode teletext and other VBI data.

    Go to http://www.linux-projects.org/ and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libxevd" to configure to enable it.

    ZVBI

    ZVBI is a VBI decoding library which can be used by FFmpeg to decode DVB teletext pages and DVB teletext subtitles.

    Go to http://sourceforge.net/projects/zapping/ and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass "--enable-libzvbi" to configure to enable it.
